question: A 4-month-old boy is brought to the physician for a well-child examination. He was born at 36 weeks' gestation. The mother has had no prenatal care. His 6-year-old sister has a history of osteosarcoma. He is exclusively breast fed. He is at the 60th percentile for height and weight. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows inward deviation of the right eye. Indirect ophthalmoscopy shows a white reflex in the right eye and a red reflex in the left eye. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Inward deviation of the right eye" -> "White reflex in the right eye" -> "Red reflex in the left eye" -> "Suspicion of retinoblastoma" -> "Fundus examination" -> 80% CHAIN: "Exclusively breastfed" -> "Risk of galactosemia due to galactose exposure" -> "Screen for galactosemia" -> 70% CHAIN: "Family history of osteosarcoma" -> "Concern for genetic predisposition to cancer" -> "Evaluate for genetic syndromes associated with retinoblastoma" -> "Fundus examination" -> 75% CHAIN: "No prenatal care" -> "Risk of congenital infections" -> "Serum rubella titers" -> 80%
analysis: The presence of a white reflex in the right eye on ophthalmoscopy is concerning for retinoblastoma, a malignant tumor of the retina. Given the family history of osteosarcoma in the sibling, there may be a genetic predisposition to cancer. Therefore, the most appropriate next step in management would be a fundus examination to further evaluate the white reflex and confirm the diagnosis of retinoblastoma.
